title: veridict verify-run report
description: JSON output of `veridict verify-run manifest.toml games.jsonl`. Not verdict-shaped (no pass/fail/inconclusive) - its own binary judgment instead, reusing the existing Validity enum directly: valid iff violations is empty. Exit code 0 for valid, 1 for invalid (one or more violations found); exit 3 (no report produced) is reserved for a genuine parse/config error - malformed manifest.toml, an unsupported manifest_schema_version, a manifest declaring nothing to verify, malformed games.jsonl, or empty input.

schema_version.description: Same REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION every other report uses - stays 1 across additive changes.

validity.description: Valid iff violations is empty. No verdict-shaped three-way concept applies here - a structural invariant either holds or it doesn't, there's no 'inconclusive'.

violations.description: Sorted deterministically, then capped at 500 entries - see violation_count/violations_truncated for the exact total when this list was cut short.

violation_count.description: Exact total violation count, even when violations above was truncated. validity/reason are derived from this, never from violations.length.

violations_truncated.description: true iff violation_count exceeds the 500-entry cap on violations above, i.e. that array is a deterministic (first-500-after-sort) sample, not the full list.

warnings.description: Human-readable mirror of checks_skipped, same 'one computation, two representations' idiom Report.data_quality/warnings already use.

paired_count.description: Count of id-groups with exactly 2 records, excluding burn-in pairs (either record marked include_in_gate: false) - the formal, gated pair count. Distinct from sprt-report.schema.json's paired_count, which counts pairs a pentanomial LLR walk actually analyzed.

manifest.description: The whole manifest.toml, echoed back verbatim - see manifest.schema.json.

lines.description: 1+ offending line numbers - plural because most violations here are relational (implicating two or more records), unlike a single-line schema-mismatch error.
